name: Hillel
overview: Hillel is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Abdon, as recorded in Judges 12:13. There is no additional tribal affiliation or notable personal details provided about him in Scripture. His mention is brief and focused on his paternal relationship.
namesAndTitles: The name Hillel means "he has praises," reflecting a Hebrew origin. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaning that highlights praise or commendation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hillel as the father of Abdon, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, there are no further family connections or relationships recorded for Hillel.
scriptureSignificance: Hillel’s significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his role as the father of Abdon, a judge of Israel. His mention in Judges 12:13 links him to the period of the judges, a critical era in Israel’s history before the monarchy. While Hillel himself is not described in detail, his lineage contributes to the record of leadership and deliverance in Israel.
